const record = `STAGE: idea submitted (ideation_1, round_20261028_233100_128)
GOAL: produce exactly one in-scope idea coupling training-only behaviour with hyperbolic geometry inside the RQ-VAE SID construction, materially different from the 3 earlier rounds.
WHAT I READ: the round objective, the 5-part scope contract, the frozen-budget experiment policy, and the failure list of rounds 125823_958 (fork-angle/angular-barycenter/radial-volume/shell/cone transport), 212003_968 (BRANCHCURV, GEO-SHELL, GEOPFX, GEO_REPAIR, KAPPA_BRANCH, LORENTZ_CONE, SUCC-TAN-RQ, behaviour-anchored charts), 221240_652 (CURVCELL, SUCCFAN-CURV, cocond-markov-poincare-ot = successor-diffused assignment mass in a Poincare Sinkhorn quantizer). All earlier arms are either assignment-side (Sinkhorn/voronoi/curvature-cell), transport-side (tangent/fork/shell), or chart-side (anchored geodesic charts).
OBSERVATION: every prior arm places the geometry on the ENCODER-SIDE assignment or on a transported coordinate frame. None placed the curved operation on the CODEBOOK PARAMETER UPDATE driven by the transition graph, i.e. on the gradient that moves code vectors rather than on the distance that assigns items to them.
REASONING: so I chose a fourth, disjoint position: a behaviour-weighted geodesic triplet margin acting only on the codebook table, using prefix-truncated Poincare distances (levels 1, 2, L) so the term directly shapes the prefix an autoregressive recommender emits. Behaviour enters as a per-transition weight that multiplies the margin violation, so behaviour-off (w=0) gives exactly zero gradient and geometry-off (Euclidean) keeps the identical term structure. Curvature and both margins are measured at epoch 0 and frozen, so nothing is tuned and no arm is repeated.
EVIDENCE: no file artifacts; the deliverable is the answer block below.
STILL OPEN: whether codebook-only gradient (no direct encoder gradient) is enough to move SIDs fast enough inside 3000 epochs; the geometry-off arm is what would answer it, but no arm is run this round.

ANSWER BLOCK (final):
IDEA: SUCC-GEO-CBTAB
TITLE: Behaviour-weighted geodesic triplet margin that moves the shared RQ codebook table so successor items' hierarchical code prefixes are Poincare-close
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built for reconstruction, not for transitions. Two items a user actually moves between often land on unrelated prefixes, so the generative recommender must memorise the transition instead of reading it off the code tree. The fix cannot be "add a graph loss", because a flat Euclidean graph loss just pulls code vectors together and collapses the codebook; the natural geometry for a tree-shaped prefix code with exponentially growing frontier is negative curvature.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds put curvature on the assignment (Sinkhorn/voronoi/curvature cells), on transported tangent frames (fork angle, shell, cone), or on anchored charts. This one leaves the assignment, the encoder and the Sinkhorn machinery completely untouched and puts the curved operation on the CODEBOOK UPDATE: a curvature-measured geodesic triplet margin over prefix-truncated code sums, with the margin violation weighted by a row-normalised transition strength. It is a code-table geometry, not an assignment geometry, not a transport, not a chart, and not an auxiliary hyperbolic head on the encoder.
CHANGE: After each epoch we snapshot every training item's three code indices (free: they come from the forward passes already run). Each step we sample transitions from the training-only successor table, form prefix code sums at levels 1, 2 and L, map them by exp_0^k into a Poincare ball of fixed curvature -k, and apply a softplus triplet margin in which the positive/negative geodesic gap is multiplied by the transition weight; gradient flows into the codebooks only.
SPECIFICATION: see SPEC EQUATIONS.
COST: No extra forward passes and no extra encoder compute. Per step: 1024 sampled transitions x 3 prefix depths x 2 distances (positive and negative) = 6144 Poincare distance evaluations at dimension d (64-128), about 0.5 MFLOP, plus 3 gather-sums over 3 tables per endpoint -> under 0.5 percent of one optimizer step at the frozen scale. Cache refresh is O(24556 x 3) integer writes once per epoch (72000 steps in total across 3000 epochs). Memory: 24556 x 3 int32 = 295 KB. Expected wall clock delta on four cards: under 1 percent.
HYPOTHESIS: If the successor table carries usable transition structure at the granularity of code prefixes, then a behaviour-weighted geodesic margin on the codebook should raise the fraction of transitions whose successor shares the anchor's level-1 and level-2 code (prefix successor hit rate) above the reconstruction-only baseline, and that gain should carry into Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 without any change to the Stage 3 protocol. Observed through: successor-prefix hit rate per level, codebook usage entropy, mean geodesic distance of true successor pairs versus random pairs, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 on the single run.
RISKS: Codebook-only gradient may be too slow to relocate codes within 3000 epochs, leaving SIDs nearly identical to baseline. Negative sampling noise could pull unrelated items together if the transition table is sparse (cold items with one transition). The behaviour weight can push duplicates into the table (two items sharing all three codes), which would help the margin but destroy SID uniqueness and hurt generation; the level-L uniqueness guard and a duplicate-count diagnostic cover this. Finally, curvature derived from the latent scale can be too flat if code sums sit very near the origin, making the Poincare distance numerically close to Euclidean.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions with row-normalised strength, computed as consecutive co-consumption inside a training session, used as a per-edge weight and as a negative-sampling constraint.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage 2 training split only. For every training session (ordered item list) and every adjacent pair (i_t, i_{t+1}) with both items in the 24556-item training vocabulary, increment T[i_t, i_{t+1}]. Then for each anchor i set w_ij = T[i,j] / max_{j'} T[i,j'], so w in (0,1] and the strongest successor of every anchor gets 1.0. Anchors with out-degree 0 are excluded. N(i) = {j : T[i,j] > 0}. The table is built once before training and never rebuilt from model state.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition table is built exclusively from training-split sessions; validation and test interactions are never read by the table builder, never enter the cache of code indices (which is filled only from training-item forward passes), and never appear as anchors, positives or negatives. Validation/test items absent from the training vocabulary are not in the cache, so they cannot enter the margin. The mechanism touches only Stage 2 (the RQ-VAE); the Stage 3 protocol and its split stay frozen and untouched, and the SID construction sees only the training graph, so no validation or test interaction can influence a code assignment.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature -k with k = 1/s^2, s^2 = mean_i ||z_i_hat||^2 measured at the end of epoch 0 and frozen. Operations: exp_0^k(v) = tanh(sqrt(k)||v||) * v / (sqrt(k)||v||) into the open unit ball, Moebius addition, and the Poincare distance d_k(u,v) = (2/sqrt(k)) * artanh(sqrt(k) * ||(-u) (+) v||).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Entirely in the quantization stage, as a gradient on the shared codebook parameters C_1..C_L of the RQ-VAE. The encoder, the nearest-code assignment rule, the decoder, the commitment loss and the reconstruction loss are all unchanged.
COUPLING PATH: w_ij (behaviour) multiplies the softplus of a geodesic gap (geometry) on prefix code sums drawn from the codebook table; the resulting gradient is the only thing that moves the codebook away from its reconstruction optimum, hence it is the single path by which both signals reach the SID. Setting w to zero removes every gradient of the term (behaviour-off is exactly the baseline trajectory); replacing d_k with the Euclidean norm changes the direction and scale of every codebook update while keeping the same term structure (geometry-off). Neither replacement leaves the other intact because w and d_k appear multiplied inside the same softplus argument.
COUPLING EQUATION: L_succ = mean over sampled (i,j) of softplus( w_ij * [ D_ij - D_ijminus + m0^2 ] ), where D_ij = (1/3) sum_{h in {1,2,L}} d_k^2( p_i^(h), p_j^(h) ), p_i^(h) = exp_0^k( sum_{l<=h} C_l[ k_l(i) ] ), and m0^2 is the measured mean geodesic distance between random code pairs.
OBSERVABLES: (a) successor-prefix hit rate at levels 1 and 2 versus the baseline; (b) mean d_k for true successor pairs relative to random pairs (separation ratio); (c) codebook usage entropy and the number of exact 3-code duplicates; (d) Stage 3 test_recall@10. All diagnostics are recorded, none is an admission gate; the single run's test_recall@10 decides.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: w_ij is set to 0 for all edges (the transition sampler is replaced by a constant-zero weight). L_succ then has value mean(log 2) and exactly zero gradient, so the run reproduces the baseline RQ-VAE trajectory bit-for-bit up to non-determinism; the switch exists in code but is not run this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: k is disabled and d_k^2(u,v) is replaced in the same equation by || z_i^(<=h) - z_j^(<=h) ||^2 (Euclidean, with m0^2 recomputed as the Euclidean counterpart at epoch 0). Same sampler, same weights, same softplus, same prefix depths.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full term with row-normalised w_ij and Poincare d_k at the measured curvature -1/s^2, added to the unchanged RQ-VAE loss with weight 1 (dimensionless because numerator and m0^2 share units). This is the only arm trained in this round.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  # --- once, before training ---
  T = zeros(N, N);  for each train session s: for t: if s[t], s[t+1] in vocab: T[s[t], s[t+1]] += 1
  N(i) = {j : T[i,j] > 0};  out_i = sum_j T[i,j]
  w[i, j] = T[i,j] / max_{j'} T[i,j']            # in (0, 1]
  # --- end of epoch 0, frozen for the rest of training ---
  zhat_i = sum_{l=1..L} C_l[k_l(i)]               # from cached training code indices
  s2 = mean_i ||zhat_i||^2 ;  kappa = 1.0 / s2
  m0_sq = mean over 10000 random training pairs (i,j) of d_kappa^2(p_i^(L), p_j^(L))
  # --- every step ---
  S = sample 1024 (i, j) pairs with T[i,j] > 0
  for (i, j) in S:
      jm = uniform item with T[i,jm] == 0 and jm not in {i, j};  resample up to 5 times, else drop the pair
      for h in (1, 2, L):
          u_i = exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(i)])       # k_l(*) from the epoch cache, integer gather
          D_ij     += (1/3) * d_kappa^2(u_i, exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(j)]))
          D_ijm    += (1/3) * d_kappa^2(u_i, exp0(sum_{l<=h} C_l[k_l(jm)]))
      loss_succ += softplus( w[i,j] * (D_ij - D_ijm + m0_sq) )
  L = L_RQVAE + loss_succ / max(1, |S_kept|)
  backward; step
  # --- end of every epoch ---
  overwrite cache k_1..k_L for all 24556 training items with the argmin indices produced by that epoch's forward passes (no extra forward pass)
  # curvature kappa is NEVER recomputed after epoch 0
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: the precomputed sparse transition table T and row-normalised weights w (training split only), the epoch cache of code indices k_l(i) for the 24556 training items, the shared codebook parameters C_1..C_L, and the two frozen scalars kappa and m0_sq measured at epoch 0. Output: the scalar L_succ and its gradient with respect to C_1..C_L only (the cached indices are integer constants, so no encoder gradient is taken through this path). Returns nothing else; it does not modify assignment, decoding or the SID export.
SAFEGUARDS: (1) Clamp ||v|| before exp0 so that the mapped radius stays below 1 - 1e-5 (tanh saturates to exactly 1 in float32 otherwise). (2) Clamp the artanh argument to 1 - 1e-7 and compute d_kappa in float64 for the distance only. (3) If s2 <= 1e-12, fall back to kappa = 1 and log a warning rather than dividing by zero. (4) Guard s2, kappa and m0_sq so they are finite and positive; if not, disable the term for the run and record the flag (no retuning). (5) Skip pairs with out_i = 0, with w = 0, or whose endpoints are not yet in the cache; never let an unseen item contribute. (6) Negative must not be in N(i) and must differ from i and from j; if all 5 resamples fail, drop the pair rather than using a false negative. (7) If the duplicate count (items sharing all L codes) rises above the epoch-0 baseline count, add no repulsion term (that would be a new mechanism) but record the count so the failure mode is visible. (8) Do not let w introduce a self-loop: force w[i,i] = 0. (9) L_succ is divided by the number of kept pairs so the gradient magnitude does not drift with table density. (10) kappa is frozen after epoch 0 so the curvature cannot drift toward zero and silently Euclideanise the term.
END IDEA`;
await tools.progress.append_progress({ content: record });
return "recorded";
